The expanded path, or the original path if HOME is missing or\n92\t///   the path doesn't start with \"~\"\n93\t///\n94\t/// # Examples\n95\t///\n96\t/// ```no_run\n97\t/// use needle::util::expand_tilde;\n98\t///\n99\t/// // Assuming HOME=/home/coding\n100\t/// assert_eq!(expand_tilde(\"~\"), \"/home/coding\");\n101\t/// assert_eq!(expand_tilde(\"~/foo\"), \"/home/coding/foo\");\n102\t/// assert_eq!(expand_tilde(\"/absolute/path\"), \"/absolute/path\");\n103\t/// assert_eq!(expand_tilde(\"relative/path\"), \"relative/path\");\n104\t/// ```\n105\t///\n106\t/// # Edge Cases\n107\t///\n108\t/// * \"~\" alone expands to HOME directory (when HOME is set)\n109\t/// * \"~\" alone returns \"~\" unchanged (when HOME is not set)\n110\t/// * If HOME is not set, \"~/foo\" returns \"~/foo\" unchanged\n111\t/// * No double slashes: \"~//foo\" expands to \"$HOME//foo\" (preserves user input)\n112\tpub fn expand_tilde(path: &str) -> String {\n113\t    // Check if path is exactly ~ (bare tilde)\n114\t    if path == \"~\" {\n115\t        match get_home() {\n116\t            Some(home) => return home,\n117\t            None => return path.to_string(),\n118\t        }\n119\t    }\n120\t\n121\t    // Check if path starts with ~/ (not just ~)\n122\t    if !path.starts_with(\"~/\") {\n123\t        return path.to_string();\n124\t    }\n125\t\n126\t    match get_home() {\n127\t        Some(home) => {\n128\t            // Replace \"~/\" with HOME + \"/\"\n129\t            // path[2..] skips the \"~/\" prefix\n130\t            format!(\"{}/{}\", home.trim_end_matches('/'), &path[2..])\n131\t        }\n132\t        None => path.to_string(),\n133\t    }\n134\t}\n135\t\n136\t/// Resolve the worker binary path with optional config override.\n137\t///\n138\t/// This function resolves the path to the worker binary by first checking\n139\t/// for an explicit config override, then falling back to the current executable.\n140\t///\n141\t/// # Arguments\n142\t///\n143\t/// * `worker_binary_path` - An optional path override from config. If `Some(path)`,\n144\t///   that path is used directly. If `None`, falls back to `std::env::current_exe()`.\n145\t///\n146\t/// # Returns\n147\t///\n148\t/// * `Result<PathBuf>` - The resolved binary path, or an error if resolution fails.\n149\t///\n150\t/// # Errors\n151\t///\n152\t/// * Returns an error if `worker_binary_path` is `None` and `std::env::current_exe()`\n153\t///   fails (which can happen in some restricted environments or when the binary\n154\t///   has been deleted/moved after launch).\n155\t///\n156\t/// # Examples\n157\t///\n158\t/// ```no_run\n159\t/// use needle::util::resolve_worker_binary_path;\n160\t/// use std::path::PathBuf;\n161\t///\n162\t/// // With explicit override\n163\t/// let override_path = Some(PathBuf::from(\"/custom/path/to/needle\"));\n164\t/// let resolved = resolve_worker_binary_path(override_path.as_ref())\n165\t///     .expect(\"failed to resolve binary path\");\n166\t/// assert_eq!(resolved, PathBuf::from(\"/custom/path/to/needle\"));\n167\t///\n168\t/// // Without override (uses current_exe)\n169\t/// let resolved = resolve_worker_binary_path(None)\n170\t///     .expect(\"failed to resolve current executable\");\n171\t/// ```\n172\tpub fn resolve_worker_binary_path(worker_binary_path: Option<&PathBuf>) -> Result<PathBuf> {\n173\t    if let Some(path) = worker_binary_path {\n174\t        Ok(path.clone())\n175\t    } else {\n176\t        std::env::current_exe()\n177\t            .context(\"failed to resolve worker binary path: current_exe() failed\")\n178\t    }\n179\t}\n180\t\n181\t/// Build a cargo test command with configurable timeout.\n182\t///\n183\t/// This function constructs a `std::process::Command` that runs `cargo test`\n184\t/// with a timeout wrapper. The timeout command will terminate the test if it\n185\t/// exceeds the specified duration.\n186\t///\n187\t/// The command is structured as: `timeout <seconds> cargo test --all-targets -- --nocapture`\n188\t///\n189\t/// # Arguments\n190\t///\n191\t/// * `timeout_minutes` - Optional timeout in minutes. If `None`, defaults to 30 minutes.\n192\t///\n193\t/// # Returns\n194\t///\n195\t/// * `std::process::Command` - Configured command ready for execution via `spawn()` or `status()`.\n196\t///\n197\t/// # Examples\n198\t///\n199\t/// ```no_run\n200\t/// use needle::util::build_cargo_test_command;\n201\t/// use std::process::Command;\n202\t///\n203\t/// // With default 30-minute timeout\n204\t/// let cmd = build_cargo_test_command(None);\n205\t///\n206\t/// // With custom 45-minute timeout\n207\t/// let cmd = build_cargo_test_command(Some(45));\n208\t///\n209\t/// // Execute the command\n210\t/// let status = cmd.status().expect(\"failed to execute cargo test\");\n211\t/// ```\n212\t///\n213\t/// # Timeout Behavior\n214\t///\n215\t/// - The `timeout` command will send `SIGTERM` to the cargo process when the timeout is reached.\n216\t/// - If the process does not exit within 1 second after `SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL` is sent.\n217\t/// - Exit code 124 indicates the timeout was triggered (see `timeout(1)` man page).\n218\t///\n219\t/// # Default Value\n220\t///\n221\t/// When `timeout_minutes` is `None`, the default is **30 minutes**.\n222\tpub fn build_cargo_test_command(timeout_minutes: Option<u64>) -> std::process::Command {\n223\t    let timeout_seconds = timeout_minutes.unwrap_or(30) * 60;\n224\t\n225\t    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(\"timeout\");\n226\t    cmd.arg(format!(\"{}\", timeout_seconds))\n227\t        .arg(\"cargo\")\n228\t        .arg(\"test\")\n229\t        .arg(\"--all-targets\")\n230\t        .arg(\"--\")\n231\t        .arg(\"--nocapture\");\n232\t\n233\t    cmd\n234\t}\n235\t\n236\t/// Capture the current system time in UTC as an ISO 8601 formatted string.\n237\t///\n238\t/// Returns the current UTC timestamp as an ISO 8601/RFC 3339 string.\n239\t/// The format is `2026-08-13T14:30:00Z` (UTC timezone indicated by `Z`).\n240\t///\n241\t/// This function handles all errors internally and never panics. If system\n242\t/// time is unavailable or chrono formatting fails (e.g., due to extreme\n243\t/// system clock values that overflow chrono's internal calculations), it\n244\t/// falls back to the Unix epoch timestamp (`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`) and\n245\t/// logs an error message to stderr.\n246\t///\n247\t/// # Returns\n248\t///\n249\t/// * `String` - Current UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or the epoch\n250\t///   timestamp as a fallback if time capture fails\n251\t///\n252\t/// # Fallback Behavior\n253\t///\n254\t/// When the system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n255\t/// or chrono formatting fails, this function:\n256\t/// - Returns `\"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z\"` (Unix epoch)\n257\t/// - Logs an error message to stderr with failure details\n258\t/// - Never panics, ensuring the function is safe to call in production\n259\t///\n260\t/// # Examples\n261\t///\n262\t/// ```no_run\n263\t/// use needle::util::capture_timestamp;\n264\t///\n265\t/// let now = capture_timestamp();\n266\t/// println!(\"Current UTC time: {}\", now);\n267\t/// // Output: \"2026-08-13T14:30:00Z\" (or epoch on failure)\n268\t/// ```\n269\t///\n270\t/// # Performance\n271\t///\n272\t/// This function performs a system call to get the current time and should\n273\t/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\n274\t///\n275\t/// # Error Handling\n276\t///\n277\t/// For use cases that need to distinguish between success and failure,\n278\t/// use [`capture_timestamp_result()`] instead, which returns a `Result`.\n279\tpub fn capture_timestamp() -> String {\n280\t    capture_timestamp_result().unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n281\t        eprintln!(\"Failed to capture timestamp: {}. Using epoch fallback.\", e);\n282\t        // Unix epoch as ISO 8601 timestamp (fallback when system time fails)\n283\t        \"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z\".to_string()\n284\t    })\n285\t}\n286\t\n287\t/// Capture the current system time in UTC as an ISO 8601 formatted string.\n288\t///\n289\t/// Returns the current UTC timestamp as an ISO 8601/RFC 3339 string.\n290\t/// The format is `2026-08-13T14:30:00Z` (UTC timezone indicated by `Z`).\n291\t///\n292\t/// This is the fallible version of [`capture_timestamp()`] that returns\n293\t/// a `Result` instead of handling errors internally. Use this when you\n294\t/// need to distinguish between successful timestamp capture and failures.\n295\t///\n296\t/// # Returns\n297\t///\n298\t/// * `Result<String>` - Current UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or an\n299\t///   error if time capture fails\n300\t///\n301\t/// # Errors\n302\t///\n303\t/// This function returns an error if:\n304\t/// - The system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n305\t/// - Chrono formatting fails to produce an ISO 8601 string (e.g., due to\n306\t///   extreme system clock values)\n307\t///\n308\t/// # Examples\n309\t///\n310\t/// ```no_run\n311\t/// use needle::util::capture_timestamp_result;\n312\t///\n313\t/// match capture_timestamp_result() {\n314\t///     Ok(timestamp) => println!(\"Current UTC time: {}\", timestamp),\n315\t///     Err(e) => eprintln!(\"Failed to capture timestamp: {}\", e),\n316\t/// }\n317\t/// ```\n318\t///\n319\t/// # Performance\n320\t///\n321\t/// This function performs a system call to get the current time and should\n322\t/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\n323\tpub fn capture_timestamp_result() -> Result<String> {\n324\t    // Use catch_unwind to handle any potential panics from chrono operations\n325\t    // This protects against extreme edge cases like system clock overflow\n326\t    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n327\t        let now = chrono::Utc::now();\n328\t        now.to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true)\n329\t    }));\n330\t\n331\t    match result {\n332\t        Ok(timestamp) => Ok(timestamp),\n333\t        Err(_) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n334\t            \"chrono operation panicked - possibly due to extreme system clock values\"\n335\t        )),\n336\t    }\n337\t}\n338\t\n339\t/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\n340\t///\n341\t/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\n342\t/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\"HOME\", ..)` or\n343\t/// `remove_var(\"HOME\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\n344\t/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\n345\t/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\n346\t/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\n347\t/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\n348\t/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\n349\t///\n350\t/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\n351\t/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\n352\t/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\n353\t#[cfg(test)]\n354\tpub(crate) mod test_env {\n355\t    use std::ffi::OsString;\n356\t    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\n357\t\n358\t    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\n359\t    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\n360\t\n361\t    /// Restores `HOME` and `PATH` to their captured values when dropped.\n362\t    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\n363\t        home: Option<OsString>,\n364\t        path: Option<OsString>,\n365\t    }\n366\t\n367\t    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\n368\t        fn drop(&mut self) {\n369\t            restore(\"HOME\", self.home.take());\n370\t            restore(\"PATH\", self.path.take());\n371\t        }\n372\t    }\n373\t\n374\t    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\n375\t        match value {\n376\t            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\n377\t            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\n378\t        }\n379\t    }\n380\t\n381\t    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\n382\t    ///\n383\t    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\n384\t    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\n385\t    /// registry. Unit tests that construct a `Worker` therefore registered\n386\t    /// themselves into it and raced each other (and the running fleet) on a\n387\t    /// single read-modify-write file. Every test config must point somewhere\n388\t    /// private instead.\n389\t    ///\n390\t    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\n391\t    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\n392\t    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\n393\t    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n394\t        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n395\t        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n396\t\n397\t        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\n398\t        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n399\t\n400\t        let root =\n401\t            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create test home root\"));\n402\t        let dir = root\n403\t            .path()\n404\t            .join(format!(\"home-{}\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\n405\t        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\"state\")).expect(\"failed to create test home state dir\");\n406\t        dir\n407\t    }\n408\t\n409\t    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\n410\t    ///\n411\t    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\n412\t    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\n413\t    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\n414\t    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\n415\t        let lock = ENV_LOCK\n416\t            .lock()\n417\t            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n418\t        let guard = EnvGuard {\n419\t            home: std::env::var_os(\"HOME\"),\n420\t            path: std::env::var_os(\"PATH\"),\n421\t        };\n422\t        (lock, guard)\n423\t    }\n424\t}\n425\t\n426\t#[cfg(test)]\n427\tmod tests {\n428\t /// Persist test metrics to a JSON file.\n298\t    ///\n299\t    /// ## Arguments\n300\t    ///\n301\t    /// * `output_dir` - Directory where the metrics file will be written\n302\t    /// * /// - The file cannot be written\n313\t    /// - The metrics cannot be serialized to JSON\n314\t    pub fn persist_metrics(&self, output_dir: &Path, base_name: &str) -> Result<()> {\n315\t        // {}\",\n319\t                output_dir.display()\n320\t            )\n321\t        })?;\n322\t\n323\t        // Create metrics from result\n324\t        let metrics = TestMetrics::from_result(self);\n325\t\n326\t        // Serialize to JSON\n327\t        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metrics)\n328\t            .context(\"failed to serialize test metrics     Ok(())\n343\t    }\n344\t\n345\t    /// Persist both test output and metrics.\n346\t    ///\n347\t    /// This is a convenience method that calls both `persist_output` and  }\n362\t\n363\t    /// Helper method to write content to a file.\n364\t    ///\n365\t    /// This method handles the actual file I/O and is used by both `persist_output` and `persist_metrics`.\n366\t ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n380\t\n381\t/// Basic test runner for executing cargo test commands.\n382\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n383\tpub struct TestRunner {\n384\t    /// Workspace directory where tests will be run.\n385\t    workspace: PathBuf,\n386\t    /// Timeout in seconds for test execution.\n387\t    timeout_secs: u64,\n388\t    /// Additional arguments to pass to cargo test.\n389\t    extra_args: Vec<String>,\n390\t}\n391\t\n392\timpl TestRunner {\n393\t    /// Create a new test runner for the given workspace.\n394\t    ///\n395\t    /// ## Arguments\n396\t    ///\n397\t    /// * `workspace` - Path to the workspace directory\n398\t    pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Self {\n399\t        Self {\n400\t timeout for test execution.\n407\t    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n408\t        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n409\t        self\n410\t    }\n411\t\n412\t    /// Add }\n417\t\n418\t    /// Run cargo test with the given additional arguments.\n419\t    ///\n420\t    /// ## Arguments\n421\t    ///\n422\t    /// * `args` - Additional arguments to pass to cargo test\n423\t    ///\n424\t    /// ## Returns\n425\t    ///\n426\t    /// Returns `TestResult` containing:\n427\t    /// - `status`: The test execution status (Success, Failed, CompilationFailed, TimedOut)\n428\t    /// - `stdout`: Captured stdout from test execution\n429\t    /// - `stderr`: Captured stderr from test execution\n430\t    /// - `exit_code`: Process exit code (None if killed by signal)\n431\t    ///\n432\t    /// ## Errors\n433\t    ///\n434\t    /// Returns an error if:\n435\t    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n436\t    /// - The process fails to spawn\n437\t    pub fn run_tests(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<TestResult> {\n438\t        let start = Instant::now();\n439\t\n440\t        // Capture the launch timestamp before constructing the command. The\n441\t        // helper supplies an epoch fallback if reading the system clock fails,\n442\t        // so a timestamp is retained even when command launch fails.\n443\t        let launch_timestamp = capture_timestamp();\n444\t\n445\t        // Build the command\n446\t        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n447\t        cmd.arg(\"test\");\n448\t        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n449\t        cmd.stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped());\n450\t        cmd.stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped());\n451\t\n452\t        // Add extra arguments\n453\t        for arg in &self.extra_args {\n454\t            cmd.arg(arg);\n455\t        }\n456\t\n457\t        // Add additional arguments\n458\t        for arg in args {\n459\t            cmd.arg(arg);\n460\t        }\n461\t\n462\t        // Spawn the process\n463\t        tracing::debug!(\n464\t            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n465\t            args = ?args,\n466\t            launch_timestamp = %launch_timestamp,\n467\t            \"spawning cargo test process\"\n468\t        );\n469\t\n470\t        let result = self.execute_with_timeout(cmd)?;\n471\t\n472\t        let duration = start.elapsed();\n473\t\n474\t        // Build the test result with captured output\n475\t        let test_result = match result {\n476\t            Some(output) => TestResult::from_output(output, duration),\n477\t            None => TestResult::timeout(duration),\n478\t        };\n479\t\n480\t        tracing::info!(\n481\t            status = ?test_result.status,\n482\t            duration_secs = duration.as_secs(),\n483\t            stdout_len = test_result.stdout.len(),\n484\t            stderr_len = test_result.stderr.len(),\n485\t            \"cargo test completed\"\n486\t        );\n487\t\n488\t        Ok(test_result)\n489\t    }\n490\t\n491\t    /// Execute a command with timeout protection.\n492\t    ///\n493\t    /// Returns Ok(Some(output)) if the command completes within timeout,\n494\t    /// Ok(None) if the command times out, or Err if the process fails to spawn.\n495\t    fn execute_with_timeout(&self, mut cmd: Command) -> Result<Option<Output>> {\n496\t        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n497\t\n498\t        // Spawn the process\n499\t        let mut child = cmd.spawn().context(\"failed to spawn cargo test process\")?;\n500\t\n501\t        // Wait for completion with timeout\n502\t        let start = Instant::now();\n503\t        loop {\n504\t            // Check if timeout exceeded\n505\t            if start.elapsed() > timeout {\n506\t                tracing::error!(timeout_secs = self.timeout_secs, \"cargo test timed out\");\n507\t\n508\t                // Kill the child process\n509\t                let _ = child.kill();\n510\t                let _ = child.wait();\n511\t\n512\t                return Ok(None);\n513\t            }\n514\t\n515\t            // Try to wait with a small timeout\n516\t            match child.try_wait() {\n517\t                Ok(Some(_status)) => {\n518\t                    // Process has exited\n519\t                    return Ok(Some(child.wait_with_output()?));\n520\t                }\n521\t                Ok(None) => {\n522\t                    // Still running, sleep a bit and retry\n523\t                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n524\t                }\n525\t                Err(e) => {\n526\t                    return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"error waiting for cargo test: {}\", e))\n527\t                        .context(\"failed to wait for cargo test process\");\n528\t                }\n529\t            }\n530\t        }\n531\t    }\n532\t\n533\t    /// Get the workspace directory.\n534\t    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n535\t        &self.workspace\n536\t    }\n537\t\n538\t    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n539\t    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n540\t        self.timeout_secs\n541\t    }\n542\t\n543\t    /// Get the extra arguments.\n544\t    pub fn extra_args(&self) -> &[String] {\n545\t        &self.extra_args\n546\t pub fn to_data(&self) -> serde_json::Value {\n        match self {\n            EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason,\n                beads_processed,\n                uptime_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                    \"uptime_secs\": uptime_secs,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                error_type,\n                error_message,\n                beads_processed,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerExhausted {\n                cycle_count,\n                last_strand,\n                waterfall_restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"cycle_count\": cycle_count,\n                    \"last_strand_evaluated\": last_strand,\n                    \"waterfall_restarts\": waterfall_restarts,\n                    \"restart_triggers\": restart_triggers,\n                    \"strand_evaluations\": strand_evaluations,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerIdle { backoff_seconds } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"backoff_seconds\": backoff_seconds })\n            }\n            EventKind::StateTransition { from, to } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"from\": format!(\"{from}\"), \"to\": format!(\"{to}\") })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepStarted { step } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepCompleted { step, duration_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step, \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerLaunchDeferred {\n                deferred_count,\n                total_wait_secs,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"deferred_count\": deferred_count,\n                    \"total_wait_secs\": total_wait_secs,\n                    \"reason\": reason\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                strand_name,\n                result,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"result\": result,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                strand_name,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"strand_name\": strand_name, \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadStoreError {\n                strand_name,\n                operation,\n                error_message,\n                stderr,\n                exit_code,\n                workspace,\n            } => {\n                let mut data = serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"operation\": operation,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"stderr\": stderr,\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                });\n                if let Some(ws) = workspace {\n                    if let Some(obj) = data.as_object_mut() {\n                        obj.insert(\"workspace\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(ws));\n                    }\n                }\n                data\n            }\n            EventKind::QueueEmpty => serde_json::json!({}),\n            EventKind::PluckStarvationDetected {\n                workspace,\n                open_count,\n                excluded_count,\n                candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"workspace\": workspace,\n                    \"open_count\": open_count,\n                    \"excluded_count\": excluded_count,\n                    \"candidate_exclusion_reasons\": candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimAttempt { bead_id, attempt } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"attempt\": attempt })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                bead_id,\n                priority,\n                strand,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"priority\": priority,\n                    \"strand\": strand,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLost { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref() })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLostSkipped {\n                consecutive_losses,\n                threshold,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"consecutive_losses\": consecutive_losses,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleased { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadCompleted {\n                bead_id,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadOrphaned { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref() })\n            }\n            EventKind::DispatchStarted {\n                bead_id,\n                agent,\n                prompt_len,\n                template_name,\n                template_version,\n                prompt_hash,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"agent\": agent,\n                    \"prompt_len\": prompt_len,\n                    \"template_name\": template_name,\n                    \"template_version\": template_version,\n                    \"prompt_hash\": format!(\"sha256:{prompt_hash}\"),\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::DispatchCompleted {\n                bead_id,\n                exit_code,\n                duration_ms,\n                agent,\n                model,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                    \"agent\": agent,\n                    \"model\": model,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RoutingDecision {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                matched_rule,\n                chosen_adapter,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"matched_rule\": matched_rule,\n                    \"chosen_adapter\": chosen_adapter,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RoutingFailed {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                rules_tried,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"rules_tried\": rules_tried,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::AgentTimeout { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> (bool, Vec<CompilationError>) {\n504\t    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n505\t    let mut errors = Vec::new();\n506\t\n507\t    // Cargo compilation           let error = CompilationError::from_error_line(line);\n520\t            errors.push(error);\n521\t            continue;\n522\t        }\n523\t\n524\t        // Check for \"could not compile\"      let message = line.trim().to_string();\n529\t            errors.push(CompilationError::new(None, message, None, None, None));\n530\t            continue;\n531\t        }\n532\t\n533\t        // errors.push(CompilationError::new(None, message, None, None, None));\n539\t            }\n540\t            continue;\n541\t        }\n542\t\n543\t        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n544\t        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n545\t            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n546\t                compilation_failed = true;\n550\t                let error = CompilationError::new(\n551\t                    Some(\"unused\".to_string()),\n552\t                    line.to_string(),\n553\t                    None,\n554\t                    None,\n555\t                    None,\n556\t                );\n557\t                errors.push(error);\n558\t \"error[\"\n575\t            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n576\t                                                  // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n577\t {\n819\t                tracing::warn!(\n820\t                    test_name = %test_name,\n821\t                    error = %e,\n822\t                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n823\t                );\n824\t            }\n825\t\n826\t            // Write stderr\n827\t            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n828\t                tracing::warn!(\n829\t    );\n843\t            }\n844\t\n845\t            tracing::info!(\n846\t                test_name = %test_name,\n847\t                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n848\t JSON value.\n    pub fn to_data(&self) -> serde_json::Value {\n        match self {\n            EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason,\n                beads_processed,\n                uptime_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                    \"uptime_secs\": uptime_secs,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                error_type,\n                error_message,\n                beads_processed,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerExhausted {\n                cycle_count,\n                last_strand,\n                waterfall_restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"cycle_count\": cycle_count,\n                    \"last_strand_evaluated\": last_strand,\n                    \"waterfall_restarts\": waterfall_restarts,\n                    \"restart_triggers\": restart_triggers,\n                    \"strand_evaluations\": strand_evaluations,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerIdle { backoff_seconds } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"backoff_seconds\": backoff_seconds })\n            }\n            EventKind::StateTransition { from, to } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"from\": format!(\"{from}\"), \"to\": format!(\"{to}\") })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepStarted { step } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepCompleted { step, duration_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step, \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerLaunchDeferred {\n                deferred_count,\n                total_wait_secs,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"deferred_count\": deferred_count,\n                    \"total_wait_secs\": total_wait_secs,\n                    \"reason\": reason\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                strand_name,\n                result,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"result\": result,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                strand_name,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"strand_name\": strand_name, \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadStoreError {\n                strand_name,\n                operation,\n                error_message,\n                stderr,\n                exit_code,\n                workspace,\n            } => {\n                let mut data = serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"operation\": operation,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"stderr\": stderr,\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                });\n                if let Some(ws) = workspace {\n                    if let Some(obj) = data.as_object_mut() {\n                        obj.insert(\"workspace\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(ws));\n                    }\n                }\n                data\n            }\n            EventKind::QueueEmpty => serde_json::json!({}),\n            EventKind::PluckStarvationDetected {\n                workspace,\n                open_count,\n                excluded_count,\n                candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"workspace\": workspace,\n                    \"open_count\": open_count,\n                    \"excluded_count\": excluded_count,\n                    \"candidate_exclusion_reasons\": candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimAttempt { bead_id, attempt } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"attempt\": attempt })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                bead_id,\n                priority,\n                strand,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"priority\": priority,\n                    \"strand\": strand,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLost { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref() })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLostSkipped {\n                consecutive_losses,\n                threshold,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"consecutive_losses\": consecutive_losses,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleased { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadOrphaned { bead_id } => {\n      }\n            EventKind::RoutingDecision {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                matched_rule,\n                chosen_adapter,\n            } => {\n Blanket impl for Arc-wrapped sinks.\n/// This enables Arc<Sink> to be used wherever Sink is required.\nimpl<T: Sink + ?Sized> Sink for Arc<T> {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Human-readable, color-coded telemetry sink for interactive monitoring.\n///\n/// Format: `HH:MM:SS [worker] EVENT detail`\npub struct StdoutSink {\n    format: StdoutFormat,\n    use_color: bool,\n}\n\nimpl StdoutSink {\n    /// Create a new stdout sink from config.\n    pub fn new(config: &StdoutSinkConfig) -> Self {\n        let use_color = match config.color {\n            ColorMode::Always => true,\n            ColorMode::Never => false,\n            ColorMode::Auto => atty_stdout(),\n        };\n        StdoutSink {\n            format: config.format,\n            use_color,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format a single event as a human-readable line.\n    pub fn format_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let time = event.timestamp.format(\"%H:%M:%S\");\n        let worker = &event.worker_id;\n        let etype = &event.event_type;\n\n        // Build the summary portion based on event type.\n        let summary = self.event_summary(event);\n\n        match self.format {\n            StdoutFormat::Minimal => {\n                let line = format!(\"{time} [{worker}] {etype}\");\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Normal => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let summary_part = if summary.is_empty() {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" ({summary})\")\n                };\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{summary_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Verbose => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let data_part = if event.data.is_object()\n                    && event.data.as_object().map_or(true, |m| m.is_empty())\n                {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" {}\", event.data)\n                };\n                let dur = event\n                    .duration_ms\n                    .map(|d| format!(\" {}ms\", d))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{dur}{data_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shorten the dotted event type to an uppercase action word.\n    fn short_type(event_type: &str) -> &str {\n        match event_type {\n            \"worker.started\" => \"STARTED\",\n            \"worker.stopped\" => \"STOPPED\",\n            \"worker.errored\" => \"ERROR\",\n            \"worker.exhausted\" => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n            \"worker.idle\" => \"IDLE\",\n            \"worker.state_transition\" => \"STATE\",\n            \"worker.queue_empty\" => \"QUEUE_EMPTY\",\n            \"strand.evaluated\" => \"STRAND\",\n            \"strand.skipped\" => \"STRAND_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.attempted\" => \"CLAIMING\",\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => \"CLAIMED\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost\" => \"RACE_LOST\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost_skipped\" => \"RACE_LOST_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.failed\" => \"CLAIM_FAIL\",\n            \"bead.released\" => \"RELEASED\",\n            \"bead.completed\" => \"COMPLETED\",\n            \"bead.orphaned\" => \"ORPHANED\",\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => \"DISPATCHED\",\n            \"agent.completed\" => \"AGENT_DONE\",\n            \"outcome.classified\" => \"OUTCOME\",\n            \"outcome.handled\" => \"HANDLED\",\n            \"heartbeat.emitted\" => \"HEARTBEAT\",\n            \"peer.stale\" => \"PEER_STALE\",\n            \"peer.crashed\" => \"PEER_CRASHED\",\n            \"health.check\" => \"HEALTH\",\n            \"effort.recorded\" => \"EFFORT\",\n            \"budget.warning\" => \"BUDGET_WARN\",\n            \"budget.stop\" => \"BUDGET_STOP\",\n            \"rate_limit.wait\" => \"RATE_WAIT\",\n            \"rate_limit.allowed\" => \"RATE_OK\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.evaluated\" => \"MITOSIS_EVAL\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.split\" => \"MITOSIS\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.skipped\" => \"MITOSIS_SKIP\",\n            \"mend.orphaned_lock_removed\" => \"MEND_LOCK\",\n            \"mend.dependency_cleaned\" => \"MEND_DEP\",\n            \"mend.db_repaired\" => \"MEND_REPAIR\",\n            \"mend.db_rebuilt\" => \"MEND_REBUILD\",\n            \"mend.cycle_summary\" => \"MEND_DONE\",\n            \"telemetry.sink_error\" => \"SINK_ERR\",\n            other => other,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Produce a brief summary from the event data.\n    fn event_summary(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let d = &event.data;\n        match event.event_type.as_str() {\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => String::new(),\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => d[\"agent\"]\n                .as_str()\n                .map(|a| format!(\"agent={a}\"))\n                .unwrap_or_default(),\n            \"agent.completed\" => {\n                let exit = d[\"exit_code\"].as_i64().unwrap_or(-1);\n                let dur = d[\"duration_ms\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"exit={exit}, {}\", format_duration_ms(dur))\n            }\n            \"outcome.classified\" => d[\"outcome\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n            \"outcome.handled\" => {\n                let outcome = d[\"outcome\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let action = d[\"action\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                format!(\"{outcome} → {action}\")\n            }\n            \"effort.recorded\" => {\n                let agent = d[\"agent_name\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let cost = d[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64();\n                let dur = d[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                match cost {\n                    Some(c) => format!(\"{agent}, {}, ${c:.4}\", format_duration_ms(dur)),\n                    None => format!(\"{agent}, {}\", format_duration_ms(dur)),\n                }\n            }\n            \"worker.stopped\" => {\n                let reason = d[\"reason\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let beads = d[\"beads_processed\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"{reason}, {beads} beads\")\n            }\n            \"worker.errored\" => d[\"error_message\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n            \"worker.idle\" => {\n                let secs = d[\"backoff_seconds\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"backoff {secs}s\")\n            }\n            \"bead.mitosis.split\" => {\n                let created = d[\"children_created\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"{created} children\")\n            }\n            \"budget.warning\" | \"budget.stop\" => {\n                let cost = d[\"daily_cost\"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);\n                let thresh = d[\"threshold\"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);\n                format!(\"${cost:.2}/${thresh:.2}\")\n            }\n            _ => String::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Wrap text in ANSI color based on event type category.\n    fn colorize(&self, event_type: &str, text: &str) -> String {\n        let code = match event_type {\n            t if t.starts_with(\"worker.errored\") || t.starts_with(\"budget.stop\") => \"\\x1b[31m\", // red\n            t if t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.succeeded\") || t == \"bead.completed\" => \"\\x1b[32m\", // green\n            t if t.starts_with(\"agent.\") || t.starts_with(\"outcome.\") => \"\\x1b[36m\", // cyan\n            t if t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.race_lost\")\n                || t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.race_lost_skipped\")\n                || t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.failed\")\n                || t == \"bead.released\"\n                || t == \"bead.orphaned\" =>\n            {\n                \"\\x1b[33m\"\n            } // yellow\n            t if t.starts_with(\"budget.warning\") || t.starts_with(\"rate_limit\") => \"\\x1b[33m\", // yellow\n            t if t.starts_with(\"mend.\") || t.starts_with(\"peer.\") => \"\\x1b[35m\", // magenta\n            t if t.starts_with(\"heartbeat\") || t.starts_with(\"health\") => \"\\x1b[90m\", // dim\n            _ => \"\\x1b[0m\",                                                      // reset / default\n        };\n        format!(\"{code}{text}\\x1b[0m\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for StdoutSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let line = self.format_event(event);\n        println!(\"{line}\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        std::io::stdout().flush()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if stdout is a terminal (for auto color detection).\nfn atty_stdout() -> bool {\n    unsafe { libc_isatty(1) != 0 }\n}\n\nextern \"C\" {\n    #[link_name = \"isatty\"]\n    fn libc_isatty(fd: i32) -> i32;\n}\n\n/// Public wrapper for formatting milliseconds as human-readable duration.\npub fn format_duration_ms_public(ms: u64) -> String {\n    format_duration_ms(ms)\n}\n\n/// Format milliseconds as human-readable duration.\nfn format_duration_ms(ms: u64) -> String {\n    if ms < 1000 {\n        format!(\"{ms}ms\")\n    } else if ms < 60_000 {\n        format!(\"{:.1}s\", ms as f64 / 1000.0)\n    } else {\n        let mins = ms / 60_000;\n        let secs = (ms % 60_000) / 1000;\n        format!(\"{mins}m{secs}s\")\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Session ID generation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Generate an 8-hex-char session ID.\n///\n/// Uses `/dev/urandom` when available, falls back to PID XOR timestamp.\npub fn generate_session_id() -> String {\n    // Try /dev/urandom (Linux/macOS)\n    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open(\"/dev/urandom\") {\n        use std::io::Read;\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 4];\n        if f.read_exact(&mut buf).is_ok() {\n            return format!(\"{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}\", buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]);\n        }\n    }\n    // Fallback: PID XOR nanosecond timestamp\n    let pid = std::process::id();\n    let ts = Utc::now().timestamp_millis() as u64;\n    let hash = pid as u64 ^ ts;\n    format!(\"{:08x}\", hash & 0xffff_ffff)\n}\n\n// ─── Trace context helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Returns `(trace_id_hex, span_id_hex)` from the current OTel span context,\n/// or `(None, None)` when not inside a valid span.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    use opentelemetry::trace::TraceContextExt;\n    let ctx = opentelemetry::Context::current();\n    let binding = ctx.span();\n    let span_ctx = binding.span_context();\n    if span_ctx.is_valid() {\n        (\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.trace_id().to_bytes())),\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.span_id().to_bytes())),\n        )\n    } else {\n        (None, None)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    (None, None)\n}\n\n// ─── HookSink ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A compiled hook: a pre-compiled regex filter + dispatch target(s).\nstruct CompiledHook {\n    filter: regex::Regex,\n    /// Shell command (empty = disabled).\n    command: String,\n    /// Webhook URL (None = disabled).\n    url: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Dispatches matching telemetry events to external commands and/or URLs.\n///\n/// Each hook has a glob pattern matched against `event_type`. When an event\n/// matches, the event JSON is piped to `command`'s stdin and/or HTTP-POSTed\n/// to `url`. Execution is fire-and-forget — failed hooks emit `SinkError`\n/// events to the file sink but never block the worker or recurse into hooks.\npub struct HookSink {\n    hooks: Vec<CompiledHook>,\n}\n\nimpl HookSink {\n    /// Compile hook configs into a `HookSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if any `event_filter` is an invalid glob pattern.\n    pub fn new(configs: &[crate::config::HookConfig]) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut hooks = Vec::with_capacity(configs.len());\n        for cfg in configs {\n            let filter = glob_to_regex(&cfg.event_filter)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid hook filter: {}\", cfg.event_filter))?;\n            hooks.push(CompiledHook {\n                filter,\n                command: cfg.command.clone(),\n                url: cfg.url.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(HookSink { hooks })\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether any hooks are configured.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.hooks.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Dispatch an event to all matching hooks (fire-and-forget).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of `SinkError` events for hooks that failed, so the\n    /// caller can write them to the file sink without recursion.\n    pub fn dispatch(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Vec<TelemetryEvent> {\n        // Never dispatch SinkError events to hooks — prevents recursion.\n        if event.event_type == \"telemetry.sink_error\" {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        let json = match serde_json::to_string(event) {\n            Ok(j) => j,\n            Err(_) => return Vec::new(),\n        };\n\n        let mut failures = Vec::new();\n        for hook in &self.hooks {\n            if !hook.filter.is_match(&event.event_type) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to command if configured.\n            if !hook.command.is_empty() {\n                match Self::run_hook(&hook.command, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0, // sequence is set by the emitter, not here\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_command\": hook.command,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to URL if configured.\n            if let Some(ref url) = hook.url {\n                match Self::post_url(url, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0,\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_url\": url,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        failures\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a single hook command, piping JSON to its stdin.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns `sh -c <command>` with the event JSON on stdin, waits for\n    /// completion, and returns an error if the command exits non-zero.\n    /// This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is acceptable.\n    fn run_hook(command: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n\n        let mut child = Command::new(\"sh\")\n            .arg(\"-c\")\n            .arg(command)\n            .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n            .stdout(Stdio::null())\n            .stderr(Stdio::null())\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n            // Best-effort write; ignore broken pipe if child exits early.\n            let _ = stdin.write_all(json.as_bytes());\n        }\n\n        // Wait for the child and check exit status.\n        let status = child\n            .wait()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to wait for hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if !status.success() {\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"hook exited with status {}: {command}\",\n                status.code().unwrap_or(-1)\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// HTTP POST the event JSON to a webhook URL.\n    ///\n    /// Sets `Content-Type: application/json` and applies a 10-second timeout.\n    /// Returns an error if the request fails or the server returns a non-2xx\n    /// status. This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is\n    /// acceptable.\n    fn post_url(url: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        ureq::post(url)\n            .set(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))\n            .send_string(json)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"webhook POST to {url} failed: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for HookSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let failures = self.dispatch(event);\n        for fail in &failures {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                hook_error = %fail.data,\n                original_event = %event.event_type,\n                \"telemetry hook dispatch failed\"\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        // hooks run synchronously in accept(); nothing to drain\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Telemetry emitter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Non-blocking telemetry emitter.\n///\n/// Cloning a `Telemetry` handle is cheap — it shares the same background\n/// writer and sequence counter.\n///\n/// The writer task must be started by calling `start()` from within a tokio\n/// runtime context. This is typically done at the beginning of `Worker::run()`.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Telemetry {\n    worker_id: WorkerId,\n    session_id: String,\n    sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,\n    /// Workspace of the most recently claimed bead, shared by all telemetry handles.\n    current_workspace: Arc<std::sync::RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>>,\n    /// Wrapped in Arc<Mutex<Option<...>>> so that `shutdown()` can drop the\n    /// sender explicitly (closing the channel) even while clones still exist.\n    sender: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<mpsc::UnboundedSender<WriterMessage>>>>,\n    /// Pending writer state that needs to be spawned in an async context.\n    /// This is `Some` until `start()` is called.\n    pending_writer: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<PendingWriter>>>,\n    /// JoinHandle for the background writer thread, set by `start()`.\n    /// Uses std::thread::JoinHandle (not tokio::task::JoinHandle) because the\n    /// writer runs in its own dedicated thread with its own tokio runtime,\n    /// ensuring it can process messages before the main runtime's block_on().\n    writer_handle: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>>>,\n    /// OTLP sink shutdown handle (feature-gated).\n    /// Stored separately so we can call its async shutdown method.\n    otlp_shutdown: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<OtlpShutdown>>>,\n}\n\n/// Worker identity used to populate OTLP resource attributes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct TelemetryIdentity {\n    /// The configured worker agent or harness name.\n    pub agent: Option<String>,\n    /// The resolved model identifier, when the adapter declares one.\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    /// The worker's workspace. OTLP sinks reduce this to its basename before export.\n    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n}\n\n/// Internal message type for the writer task.\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\nenum WriterMessage {\n    Event(TelemetryEvent),\n    Flush(tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>),\n}\n\n/// Holds the receiver and sinks until they can be spawned in an async context.\nstruct PendingWriter {\n    receiver: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<WriterMessage>,\n    sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>,\n}\n\n/// Holds an OTLP sink for async shutdown (feature-gated).\nenum OtlpShutdown {\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    Sink(std::sync::Arc<crate::telemetry::OtlpSink>),\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n    None,\n}\n\nimpl OtlpShutdown {\n    /// Shutdown the OTLP sink gracefully.\n    ///\n    /// This drains all batched exports before returning.\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        match self {\n            OtlpShutdown::Sink(sink) => {\n                // We need to extract the OtlpSink from Arc to call shutdown\n                // Try to unwrap the Arc - if there are other references, we'll force_flush instead\n                match std::sync::Arc::try_unwrap(sink) {\n                    Ok(otlp) => otlp.shutdown().await,\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\"Cannot shutdown OTLP sink: Arc has multiple references\");\n                        Ok(())\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// No-op shutdown when OTLP feature is disabled.\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Telemetry {\n    fn new_workspace_cell() -> Arc<std::sync::RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>> {\n        Arc::new(std::sync::RwLock::new(None))\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter that writes to a `FileSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from\n    /// within a tokio runtime context before emitting events.\n    ///\n    /// Writes `worker.booting` directly to the file before returning, so even\n    /// if the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL log.\n    pub fn new(worker_id: WorkerId) -> Self {\n        let session_id = generate_session_id();\n        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();\n\n        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();\n        match FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id) {\n            Ok(s) => {\n                // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.\n                // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.\n                // This ensures we have a trace even if the writer thread fails to start.\n                let version = env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\");\n                if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {\n                    // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)\n                    let error_msg = e.to_string();\n                    if error_msg.contains(\"timed out\")\n                        || error_msg.contains(\"filesystem may be hung\")\n                    {\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow\"\n                        );\n                        eprintln!(\"  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.\");\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to write boot event directly to file\");\n                }\n                sinks.push(Box::new(s));\n            }\n            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry file sink\"),\n        }\n\n        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };\n\n        Telemetry {\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            sequence,\n            current_workspace: Self::new_workspace_cell(),\n            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),\n            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),\n            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter with both file and stdout sinks.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks.
